title: When does the ID algorithm fail?
review_scope: Full paper (9 pages): Abstract, Sections 1-5, References
page_or_section_anchors: Abstract (p.1): ID algorithm is sound and complete; Corollary 3 (hedge criterion) is incorrect as stated
Section 2 (pp.2-3): Preliminaries on graphical causal models, interventional distributions, identification
Section 3 (pp.3-4): Modern presentation of ID algorithm; Corollary 3 stated formally
Section 4 (pp.4-7): Counterexample to Corollary 3; corrected graphical characterizations of ID failure
Section 5 (pp.7-8): Examples illustrating hedge structure and ID failure cases
research_question: When does the ID algorithm fail to identify interventional distributions p(Y|do(a)) in graphical causal models?
methods: Theoretical/graphical analysis: constructs counterexample to Corollary 3 (hedge criterion); provides corrected characterizations
data_or_experiment: No empirical data; pure theoretical analysis with graphical examples
main_conclusions: Corollary 3 from [Shpitser 2008] (hedge criterion) is incorrect as stated
The ID algorithm itself remains sound and complete
Corrected graphical characterizations of ID failure are provided
Hedge structure does arise when input is not identified, but the specific criterion in Corollary 3 is wrong
gap001_claim_supported: GAP-001 identification failure: demonstrates that even established identification algorithms have subtle errors in their graphical characterizations of when intervention effects are identifiable
support_type: FAILURE_CONDITION: Shows specific failure mode in causal identification — the boundary between identifiable and non-identifiable interventions is subtler than previously thought
limitations: Preprint, not peer-reviewed
Pure theoretical; no empirical validation
Focuses specifically on ID algorithm; other identification approaches not covered
claim_support_reasoning: Paper directly addresses when causal identification fails, which is a core concern of GAP-001 (intervention/control evidence layer). The correction to the hedge criterion demonstrates that identification failure boundaries require careful formal treatment.
not_supporting: Does not provide empirical evidence on intervention effects; does not address transportability or external validity

title: A Reflection on the Impact of Misspecifying Unidentifiable Causal Inference Models in Surrogate Endpoint Evaluation

review_scope: Full paper (12 pages): Abstract, Introduction, Methods (Sections 2-4), Simulation Study, Results, Conclusion

Section 2-3 (pp.3-6): Causal model for surrogate evaluation; unidentifiability of the causal model; sensitivity analysis framework
Section 4 (pp.6-9): Simulation study comparing multivariate normal vs t-distribution true models
Conclusion (p.10): Conclusions robust across different modeling assumptions; sensitivity analysis essential when models are unidentifiable
research_question: What is the impact of misspecifying unidentifiable causal models in surrogate endpoint evaluation?
methods: Simulation study: generates data from multivariate t-distribution and normal distribution; fits misspecified models; compares causal effect estimates
data_or_experiment: Monte Carlo simulation with varying sample sizes and distributional assumptions
main_conclusions: Misspecification of unidentifiable causal models leads to biased surrogate endpoint evaluation
Sensitivity analysis is essential when the causal model contains unidentifiable components
Conclusions are more robust when sensitivity analysis covers multiple modeling assumptions
The normal causal model's unidentifiability compounds the misspecification problem
gap001_claim_supported: GAP-001 boundary: demonstrates that unidentifiable causal models require explicit sensitivity analysis — this is a failure condition for intervention/control evidence
support_type: BOUNDARY: Defines the boundary between identifiable and unidentifiable intervention effects in surrogate endpoint settings
limitations: Preprint, not peer-reviewed

Focuses specifically on surrogate endpoints; generalizability to other intervention types unclear
claim_support_reasoning: Directly addresses how unidentifiable causal models affect intervention-related conclusions. The sensitivity analysis framework maps to GAP-001's need for explicit boundary treatment of identification failure.
